question: Two trains having lengths of 300 m and 200 m are running at speeds of 70 km/h and 120 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Distance = 300 + 200 = 500 m = 0.5 km

Relative Speed (same direction) = 120 − 70 = 50 km/h

Time (hours) = Distance ÷ Speed = 0.5 ÷ 50 = 1/100 hours

Time (minutes) = (1/100) × 60 = 0.6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 0.6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of slower train (L₁) = 300 m

Speed of slower train (S₁) = 70 km/h

Length of faster train (L₂) = 200 m

Speed of faster train (S₂) = 120 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time taken to cross = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₂ − S₁
